hook.line: How to sell anything to anyone.
hook.visual: Black screen with a single sales bar growing from a red $0 to a green $18,364 while the line is spoken word by word underneath.

beats.what: Sales bar starts growing from $0 and turns from red to green as the number climbs.
Big '1.' number card, then the 'framing effect' title.
Two identical yogurt cups appear, labelled '20% fat' and '80% fat-free'.
The '20% fat' cup dims and the '80% fat-free' cup glows: the better framing wins visually.
One-line takeaway text under the cups: people buy based on framing.
Bundle pricing: a single backpack with a $30 tag appears.
Side-by-side: backpack plus priced watch versus backpack with the watch tagged FREE, both $49.99.
Scarcity effect title; a shop page with a shoe and a 'buy now' button.
A red 'only 3 in stock' badge pops onto the product page.
Cursor clicks 'buy now', closing the example.

why_it_works: Result shown before the advice: the climbing sales bar is the promise, so the viewer stays to see how.
Each principle gets one simple before/after pair (dim vs glowing cup, paid vs free watch), so it reads without sound.
One motion every ~3 s (20.78 events/min) on a black background keeps the eye on a single moving object.
Three named tactics with titles make it a save-worthy cheat sheet (14.4k shares).
weaknesses: No face or voice personality; the account is interchangeable with any other explainer channel.
The save/follow ask lives only in the post caption, never in the video.
Empty black frames between sections (around 27 s) show nothing while the voice continues.
for_robert: Open with a growing number (a bar or counter that climbs while he says the promise), and give each tip one tiny before/after visual that Fred can point at.
